_readme: Concept bank for the Hamdam Instagram reel series. The agent READS this file and never writes to it. After a concept ships, set used=true by hand - and verify against live captions, because the flag has drifted before.
_verification_status: Persian lesson, send and insight lines are drafted by Claude and reviewed by Ealia. Arguments carry _check notes.
_page_note: Reel pages: 1 headline, 2 lesson + send/reflect prompt, 3 the philological point, 4 Persian verse, 5 English translation with poet line. Stage 0 is not rendered. insightEn, lessonEn, sendEn, englishSaid and headline are Latin script ONLY - Source Serif has no Arabic glyphs.
_english_said_rule: englishSaid is the English as a writer would say it, and page 5 shows it in preference to the queue's literal 'english'. The queue is never edited - it stays as provenance. Literal glosses like 'no room remains for the trouble of strangers' are exactly the flattening this account exists to argue against.
_sendability_test: BEFORE writing a send prompt, ask WHO THE POEM POINTS AT. (a) Points at the READER'S OWN FAILING - never sendable; use promptType 'reflect' with a question. (b) Points at SOMETHING SHARED - sendable. (c) Points WARMLY AT THE RECIPIENT - sendable. A warm prompt bolted onto a self-accusing poem reads as false.
_message_not_meditation: The deeper filter, learned 3 Sep 2026: most verses are MEDITATIONS - the poet thinking alone - and nobody forwards a meditation because there is no one it is for. The verses that get shared are already addressed to a person. Saadi's ghazals are spoken TO someone; Khayyam's quatrains are arguments with himself. Prefer verses that are messages, and where the original uses yar or dust as an addressee, translating it as second person turns a description into something a person would actually send.
_cta_principle_addendum: A send prompt that DESCRIBES the recipient is an appraisal, and appraisals do not get forwarded. Strongest forms: FIRST PERSON PLURAL ('let us not grieve yesterday and tomorrow') or SECOND PERSON ('for you who were there for it') - the sender adopts the line as their own words. Use the poem's own vocabulary.
_app_link_rule: Connect a verse to the app ONLY where the connection is real. saadi-017 works because nafas is literally the dam in ham-dam. Forcing this onto a Khayyam mortality quatrain would be an advert wearing a poem, which is the thing this format exists to avoid.
_seasonal_note: Check the hemisphere before scheduling any verse with seasonal imagery. The audience is largely Australian diaspora.
_context_rule: Only use verses whose meaning is complete in the lines shown. rumi-028 was dropped because the insight claimed something the couplet does not say.
_mood_key: happy = bright Mahur; love = romantic Mahur; grave = restrained, sparse; wry = light but not celebratory.

concepts.headline: ONE GOOD BREATH
concepts.englishSaid: Once you've had one good breath with a real friend, nothing else looks like much.
concepts.argument:
The measure is nafasi - one breath. Not a year, not a friendship. One breath. Saadi is saying the whole thing can be settled in a moment that short.

And the verb is takhayyol nakonad - does not imagine. Not "holds no worth", which is what the literal translation gives you. He is not claiming other things become worthless. He is saying the mind stops picturing them. Contentment as the absence of wandering.

Daryaft is received, not earned - the breath arrives; you do not produce it.

ham-dam: the one you share that breath with. We named the app after it.
concepts.insightFa: سعدی می‌گوید «نفسی» — یک دم. و «همدم» یعنی کسی که همان دم را با تو قسمت می‌کند
concepts.insightEn: Saadi says nafasi - one breath. Hamdam means the one who shares it.
concepts.lessonFa: یک لحظهٔ خوب با دوست، بقیهٔ چیزها را کوچک می‌کند
concepts.lessonEn: One good moment with a friend makes everything else look small
concepts.sendFa: برای تویی که آن لحظه با من بودی
concepts.sendEn: For you who were there for it
concepts._check: Read and chosen by Ealia 3 Sep 2026. The takhayyol nakonad reading (the mind stops imagining, rather than things losing worth) is interpretive - worth a native reader confirming. CTA is second person: the sender adopts the line as their own words. The app link is genuine here because nafas is the same dam as in ham-dam.

concepts.headline: TWO DAYS I REFUSE TO WORRY ABOUT
concepts.englishSaid: These two or three days of life have gone - like water down a stream, like wind across a plain. Two days have never cost me a moment's grief: the one not yet come, and the one already gone.
concepts.argument:
Khayyam does not say seize the day. Read the last two lines: he names two specific days and refuses both of them.

The day that has not come. The day that has gone. Those are the only two he has ever declined to grieve over - which leaves exactly one day standing, and he never has to mention it.

He does not argue for the present. He subtracts the other two and lets you notice what is left.
concepts.insightFa: خیام نمی‌گوید «دم را دریاب» — دو روز را نام می‌برد و هر دو را کنار می‌گذارد
concepts.insightEn: Khayyam never says seize the day. He names two days and refuses both, and lets you notice what is left.
concepts.lessonFa: دو روز را نمی‌شود زندگی کرد: دیروز و فردا
concepts.lessonEn: Two days cannot be lived: yesterday and tomorrow
concepts.sendFa: بیا غم دیروز و فردا را نخوریم
concepts.sendEn: Let's not grieve yesterday and tomorrow
concepts._check: PUBLISHED 2 Sep 2026 07:57 Sydney, instagram.com/reel/DcwrdcuD8Ep/ - reach 262, 1 save, 1 share, avg watch 3.2s.

concepts.headline: THE PLAN WAS NOT MADE WITH YOU
concepts.englishSaid: Why grieve over what has to be? Why wear your soul out on useless thought? Live gladly, let the world go by in joy - the plan was made without asking you.
concepts.argument:
Khayyam is not comforting you. Read the last line again: the arrangement was made without consulting you.

If the plan was never yours to approve, then the worry you are carrying about it was never doing any work. He is not saying it will be fine. He is saying your anxiety has no job here.
concepts.insightFa: خیام دلداری نمی‌دهد؛ می‌گوید تصمیم بی تو گرفته شده — و همین آزادت می‌کند
concepts.insightEn: Khayyam is not offering comfort. He says the decision was made without you - and that is what frees you.
concepts.lessonFa: بعضی چیزها را بی‌مشورت تو چیده‌اند
concepts.lessonEn: Some things were arranged without asking you
concepts.sendFa: برای کسی که با او می‌شود از نگرانی‌ها گفت
concepts.sendEn: For someone you can talk your worries through with
concepts._check: A meditation rather than a message - see _message_not_meditation. Expect weaker sharing than the Saadi verses.

concepts.headline: TOMORROW IS NOT YOURS YET
concepts.englishSaid: Tomorrow is not yours to reach, and thinking of it is only fever. Don't waste this breath, even if your heart isn't burning - no one has priced what's left of your life.
concepts.argument:
The word Khayyam uses is dastras - ordinary Persian for within reach, the word you would use about a shop or a phone. Not a philosophical term at all.

So the line is not a meditation on time. It is practical: tomorrow is not available to you. Whatever you are doing with it in your head right now, you are handling something that is not in the room.
concepts.insightFa: «دسترس» واژهٔ روزمره است، نه فلسفی — خیام می‌گوید فردا در دسترس تو نیست
concepts.insightEn: Dastras is everyday Persian for within reach. Not a philosophical claim - a practical one.
concepts.lessonFa: فردا هنوز به دست تو نیست
concepts.sendFa: برای کسی که امروز کنارت است
concepts.sendEn: For someone who is beside you today
concepts._check: dastras as everyday register is the claim to check.

concepts.headline: WHAT AUTUMN TOOK, SPRING REPAYS
concepts.englishSaid: What autumn carried off, spring comes and pays back.
concepts.argument: Rumi does not say spring is generous, or that it makes up for autumn. He says it repays - the Persian is a debt word, the one you use for settling an account. Autumn took something that was never its own to keep. Spring is not doing you a kindness; it is returning what was owed.
concepts.insightFa: ادا کردن واژهٔ بدهی است — بهار بخشش نمی‌کند، حساب صاف می‌کند
concepts.insightEn: The verb is a debt word. Spring is not being generous - it is settling an account.
concepts.lessonFa: آنچه پاییز برد، بهار پس می‌دهد
concepts.lessonEn: What autumn took, spring gives back
concepts.sendFa: برای کسی که زمستان سختی را پشت سر گذاشته
concepts.sendEn: For someone who has come through a hard winter
concepts.poetLineFa: مولانا — بلخ و قونیه، قرن سیزدهم
concepts._check: HOLD - SEASONAL. It is spring in Sydney; a line about winter ending reads as borrowed from a northern account. Schedule when the seasons match.

concepts.headline: WHY HAVE YOU FROZEN IN THAT CORNER
concepts.englishSaid: Why have you frozen in that corner? Why won't you turn too? Are you some unlucky thought that circles nothing but grief?
concepts.argument:
One verb carries this line, and it repeats: to turn.

Rumi asks why you have stopped turning - and then names the thing that has you stuck, which is not sadness itself but a thought that only ever revolves around sadness. He is not telling you to be happy. He is pointing out that you are still moving, just in a circle of one subject.
concepts.insightFa: مولانا نمی‌گوید غم نخور؛ می‌گوید تو داری می‌گردی، اما فقط دور یک چیز
concepts.insightEn: Rumi does not say stop grieving. He says you are still turning - just around one subject.
concepts.lessonEn: Turning is easier than standing still
concepts.sendFa: چه چیزی دوباره به حرکتت می‌آورد؟
concepts.poetLineFa: مولانا — بلخ و قونیه، قرن سیزدهم
concepts._check: Reflect, not send - the poem points at the reader's own stuckness.

concepts.headline: STILL NO MASTER
concepts.englishSaid: Not one day free of this world's hold. Not one breath at ease in my own life. I've been time's apprentice long enough - and I'm still no master of it.
concepts.argument:
A quatrain is built to arrive somewhere. Three lines set it up and the fourth lands.

This one refuses. Khayyam spends three lines describing a life of study and constraint, and then the fourth admits he has not learned the trade. The form promises wisdom and the content declines to supply any.
concepts.insightFa: رباعی قرار است در مصراع چهارم به حکمت برسد — این یکی اعتراف می‌کند که نرسیده
concepts.insightEn: A quatrain is built to arrive at wisdom in its fourth line. This one admits it has not.
concepts.lessonFa: سال‌ها شاگردی کردم و هنوز استاد نیستم
concepts.lessonEn: Years a student, and still no master
concepts.sendFa: تو در چه کاری هنوز شاگردی؟
concepts.sendEn: What are you still a student of?
concepts._check: Reflect, not send - a confession is not something you forward.

concepts.headline: LOOK DOWN ON NO ONE
concepts.englishSaid: We never thought it of him - and still we mocked him. Look down on no one.
concepts.argument:
Notice the order. Rumi does not begin with the advice - he begins by admitting that he was one of the people doing the taunting. Only then: look upon no human being with contempt.

Advice that arrives after a confession lands differently from advice that arrives from above.
concepts.insightFa: مولانا اول اعتراف می‌کند که خودش طعنه می‌زده — نصیحت بعد از اعتراف می‌آید
concepts.insightEn: Rumi admits he did the taunting himself. The advice comes after the confession, not from above it.
concepts.sendFa: آخرین بار کی دربارهٔ کسی زود قضاوت کردی؟
concepts.sendEn: When did you last judge someone too quickly?
concepts.poetLineFa: مولانا — بلخ و قونیه، قرن سیزدهم
concepts._check: Reflect, not send - self-accusation. Closest verse in the queue to Saadi's Bani Adam in register.
